## Settings — email pre-flight

**Send test email** sends a real message to *your own* address over the configured sign-in
mailer. It takes no recipient, so it cannot be used to relay mail. The outcome stays on the
card rather than passing by in a toast: a failure names the transport stage that broke —
connect, TLS, auth or send — and carries the request ID to search the server log by. A
success means the mailer accepted the message; if it then never arrives, the relay is the
next place to look, not this configuration.

## Settings — privacy & failing samples

**Zero-sample mode** stops failing-row samples from being stored at all: results, dry-runs,
incident evidence and alerts carry aggregates and metric values only. The toggle takes
effect on the next run — nothing has to restart. If the deployment pins the mode on in its
environment the toggle is shown pinned and can only be turned *on* from here, never off;
that is deliberate, so an operator's floor cannot be undone by a click. Every change is
audited with who made it and when. Samples stored before the switch are not deleted by it;
the retention sweep removes them on its schedule.

## Settings — scoring

**Health-score weights** are the penalties each severity tier carries when a score is
computed: `warn`, `fail` and `critical`, with `pass` fixed at zero. The defaults are
0.5 / 1.0 / 2.0; `critical` doubles as the normaliser, so an all-`fail` suite scores 50 and
an all-`critical` one scores 0. They must stay ordered (`warn ≤ fail ≤ critical`) and
`critical` must be above zero, or the save is refused with the reason.

Scores are computed when a page is read, never stored. A change therefore recolours **every**
score at once — the dashboard cards and their period-over-period deltas, the suite ranking,
asset scorecards, and any run you look at from before the change. There is no data-side
event to explain the step; the audit log carries it, with the old and new weights and who
saved them. **Reset to defaults** removes the stored row and is audited the same way.

/** Whether membership is switched on, and whether it is actually being enforced. */
export interface EnforcementState {
  /** The members table has at least one row. */
  enforcement_active: boolean;
  /** Whether any door is gated right now — false under developer bypass. */
  enforced: boolean;
  /** Why not, when `enforced` is false. */
  enforced_reason: string | null;
}

export interface MembershipView extends EnforcementState {

"""`GET /admin/workspace-config` — the read-only retention + sign-in allowlist readout."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator
from typing import Any

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
from backend.app.db.session import get_db
from backend.app.main import app

URL = "/api/v1/admin/workspace-config"


@pytest.fixture
def client(db_session: Any) -> Iterator[TestClient]:
    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: db_session
    try:
        yield TestClient(app)
    finally:
        app.dependency_overrides.clear()


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _fresh_settings() -> Iterator[None]:
    get_settings.cache_clear()
    yield
    get_settings.cache_clear()


def _set(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, **env: str) -> None:
    for key, value in env.items():
        monkeypatch.setenv(key, value)
    get_settings.cache_clear()


def _by_variable(body: dict[str, Any], key: str) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    return {row["variable"]: row for row in body[key]}


def test_reports_the_configured_retention_clocks(
    client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    _set(
        monkeypatch,
        SAMPLE_FAILURES_RETENTION_DAYS="7",
        AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS="400",
        OTP_CODES_RETENTION_HOURS="12",
    )
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    retention = _by_variable(body, "retention")
    assert (retention["SAMPLE_FAILURES_RETENTION_DAYS"]["value"], "days") == (
        7,
        retention["SAMPLE_FAILURES_RETENTION_DAYS"]["unit"],
    )
    assert retention["AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS"]["value"] == 400
    assert (retention["OTP_CODES_RETENTION_HOURS"]["value"], "hours") == (
        12,
        retention["OTP_CODES_RETENTION_HOURS"]["unit"],
    )
    assert all(row["detail"] for row in body["retention"])


def test_allowlist_for_an_unused_mode_is_shown_but_inert(
    client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    # OIDC values set with no OIDC issuer configured: no door reads them (ADR 0043), so the
    # readout must not present them as the thing keeping anyone out — or in.
    _set(
        monkeypatch,
        OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS="Ada@Example.com, grace@example.com",
        OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS="example.org",
        WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS="root@example.com",
    )
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    lists = _by_variable(body, "signup_allowlists")
    oidc = lists["OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS"]
    assert oidc["values"] == ["ada@example.com", "grace@example.com"]
    assert oidc["active"] is False
    assert lists["OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS"]["values"] == ["example.org"]
    admin = lists["WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS"]
    assert (admin["values"], admin["active"], admin["grants"]) == (
        ["root@example.com"],
        True,
        "admin_role",
    )
    assert set(lists) == {
        "OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS",
        "OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS",
        "AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS",
        "AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS",
        "WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS",
    }
    assert all(row["grants"] == "sign_in" for v, row in lists.items() if v != "WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS")


def test_allowlist_is_active_when_its_mode_gates_a_door(
    client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    _set(
        monkeypatch,
        OIDC_ISSUER="https://issuer.example.com/",
        OIDC_AUDIENCE="dataq",
        OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS="example.com",
        WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS="dev@dataq.local",
    )
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    lists = _by_variable(body, "signup_allowlists")
    assert lists["OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS"]["active"] is True
    assert lists["OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS"]["active"] is True  # same door, empty list
    assert lists["AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS"]["active"] is False
    assert body["dev_bypass_active"] is False
    assert (body["oidc_default_role"], body["otp_default_role"]) == ("member", "member")


def test_the_readout_carries_no_secret_bearing_setting(client: TestClient) -> None:
    body = client.get(URL).json()
    text = str(body).lower()
    for forbidden in ("secret", "password", "token", "key_vault", "client_secret"):
        assert forbidden not in text, forbidden


@pytest.mark.parametrize("role", ["member", "viewer"])
def test_non_admins_are_refused(
    client: TestClient, as_role: Callable[..., tuple[Any, dict[str, str]]], role: str
) -> None:
    _, headers = as_role(role)
    assert client.get(URL, headers=headers).status_code == 403

_publisher_lock = threading.Lock()


def _split_csv(raw: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Comma-separated env string → trimmed, non-empty tuple."""
    return tuple(part.strip() for part in raw.split(",") if part.strip())


def _build_publisher() -> AlertPublisher:
    """A composite over every channel (Teams · Slack · email · generic webhook).
    Each child resolves its secret + per-suite policy per run (so rotation is
    picked up) and stays a quiet no-op until configured; the registry only
    wires the store + names, never reads a secret.
    """
    settings = get_settings()
    store = get_secret_store()
    return CompositePublisher(
        [
            TeamsPublisher(
                secret_store=store,
                workspace_secret_name=settings.teams_webhook_secret_name,
            ),
            SlackPublisher(
                secret_store=store,
                webhook_secret_name=settings.slack_webhook_secret_name,
                allowed_hosts=_split_csv(settings.slack_webhook_allowed_hosts.lower()),
            ),
            EmailPublisher(
                secret_store=store,
                smtp_host=settings.email_smtp_host,
                smtp_port=settings.email_smtp_port,
                username=settings.email_username,
                password_secret_name=settings.email_password_secret_name,
                sender=settings.email_from,
                recipients=_split_csv(settings.email_to),
            ),
            # No workspace-level config — a generic webhook only ever exists as
            # a suite-linked channel (#1514/#1662), never a single default.
            WebhookPublisher(secret_store=store),
        ]
    )


def _get_publisher() -> AlertPublisher:
    """The cached composite (built once). Both seams below are views onto this one
    object — the channels and their secrets are identical, only the DTO differs.
    """
    global _publisher_singleton
    if _publisher_singleton is not None:
        return _publisher_singleton
    with _publisher_lock:
        if _publisher_singleton is None:
            _publisher_singleton = _build_publisher()
            log.info("result_publisher_initialized", impl=type(_publisher_singleton).__name__)
        return _publisher_singleton


def get_result_publisher() -> ResultPublisher:
    """Return the configured run-outcome publisher (built once, then cached)."""
    return _get_publisher()

content.content:
## Page map

| Tab | URL | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Overview | `/admin/overview` | Workspace counts — members, suites, open incidents, runs today — plus a "needs attention" feed and a workspace-health checklist, each row linking to the thing that needs fixing. |
| Members | `/admin/members` | Every user with their workspace role (editable in place) and every per-suite access grant. |
| Suites | `/admin/suites` | Every suite in the workspace, unscoped by sharing: owner, datasource, environment, check count, share count. |
| Settings | `/admin/settings` | Workspace facts and the sign-in method, the email pre-flight test, reusable notification channels, the LLM provider, zero-sample mode, the health-score weights, the secret-store notice, and the danger zone. |
| Calendar | `/admin/calendar` | The workspace's seasonal calendar: named sale and holiday periods that per-period anomaly checks can attach. |
| Compliance | `/admin/compliance` | The audit log with its filters and retention disclosure, audit-chain verification, the data-subject-rights tools, and the deployment / data-residency posture. |
| Integrations | `/admin/integrations` | Ready-to-paste inbound webhook URLs for each configured orchestration provider, with the auth mode each one uses. |

The former standalone **Settings** page has moved here: `/settings` now redirects to
`/admin/settings`, and the sidebar carries a single **Admin** entry rather than two links
to the same area.

## Who can open it
=== api-keys.md headings
1:# API keys (personal access tokens)
19:## Minting a key
52:## Using a key
65:## Listing and revoking
77:## Security properties
=== features.md headings
15:## Datasources
36:## Checks & authoring
88:## Suites

110:## Finding things — global search (⌘K / Ctrl K)
126:## Results, dashboard & history
200:## Orchestration (monitor + trigger only)
215:## Alerting
242:## Data protection
250:## Access & auth
267:## AI-assisted authoring and root-cause analysis
281:## AI assistants (MCP)
297:## Observability
303:## Deployment & portability
=== changelog fragment rules

# changelog.d — one file per change

Every PR that changes something a user, deployer or API client would notice adds **one
small file here** instead of editing `docs/site/reference/changelog.md`. The published
page renders these under **Unreleased** at build time; at release
`scripts/changelog.py assemble` moves them into a dated section and deletes them.

## Filename

```
<number>.<section>.md         e.g. 2395.changed.md
<number>-<n>.<section>.md     a second entry for the same number, e.g. 2440-2.added.md
```

- `<number>` — the issue the change belongs to (the PR number if there is no issue).
- `<n>` — `2`, `3`, … for further fragments of the same number.
- `<section>` — `breaking` | `security` | `added` | `changed` | `fixed`.

Only files matching this grammar (plus this README) may live here.

## Body

The bullet's text in Markdown, **without** the leading `- `, continuation lines unindented.
Lead with a bold phrase, as the existing entries do, and describe the behaviour — never cite
an issue or PR number, the page is public (CONTRIBUTING rule 41).

```markdown
**Changelog entries are collected one file per change.** A PR adds a fragment under
`changelog.d/` and the published page assembles them, so two PRs never conflict on the
changelog.
changelog.d/2395.changed.md
changelog.d/2443.fixed.md
changelog.d/2466.fixed.md

content.content:
## Access & auth

- **Two sign-in modes** — **email OTP** (a one-time code, no Identity Provider
  required — the local/eval default, ADR 0032) and **OIDC SSO**
  (provider-neutral, Azure AD and AWS Cognito both validated in prod). Exactly one is active per deployment.
- **Personal access tokens (PATs)** — `dq_live_` tokens for headless / AI-client use, same
  authz as the user, on REST **and** `/mcp` ([API keys](api-keys.md), ADR 0026).
- **Suite sharing** — per-suite view / edit grants, capped by workspace role (below).
- **Workspace roles — Admin / Member / Viewer** — a stored, in-app-managed role per user
  (ADR 0033), not just an env allowlist. Admin has workspace-wide visibility over every
  suite/result/schedule and is the only role that can create, edit, delete, re-auth, or
  test a **connection** — connections are shared infrastructure holding credentials, so
  Members consume them but don't manage them. Member can create/own suites and receive
  `edit` shares; Viewer is capped at `view` everywhere, including on any share. Roles are
  managed under [`/admin/members`](admin.md) by an existing Admin; `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` still works as a
  bootstrap/break-glass allowlist for a fresh or locked-out workspace.

bring back what an earlier sweep removed.

## Summary

Picks up the Profile / Workspace-Settings IA deferred in the post-v1 admin notes and replaces every labelled placeholder with real content. Theme / timezone / dark-mode stay out (ADR 0022). Also fixes the stale Settings → Notifications copy (#1840), which is the same surface.

**Profile** (`/profile`, per-user; a Viewer sees the same page read-only)
- **Your access** — the effective role in the user's own terms (Admin / Member / Viewer — a viewer no longer reads as "Member") and the caller's suites counted by access level (owned / admin / edit / view), with a note on what the count cannot see.
- **Suites you own** — alphabetical links to each owned suite, with an explained empty state.
- Both come from the caller-scoped `GET /suites` (`my_permission`) — no new endpoint. Card titles are real `h4` headings; the list carries an accessible name.

**Workspace Settings** (`/admin/settings`, Admin-only — the existing `RequireRole` gate on the parent route)
- **Sign-in access (read-only)** — each deployment allowlist (`OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS` / `_DOMAINS`, `AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS` / `_DOMAINS`, `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS`) with its values and a *worded* status: "Read at sign-in", "Not read — sign-in mode not configured" (values set for a mode the deployment does not use admit nobody — ADR 0043), or "Grants the Admin role". Plus the first-sign-in roles and a developer-bypass notice. Identifiers only, never a secret.
- **Data retention (read-only)** — `SAMPLE_FAILURES_RETENTION_DAYS`, `AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS`, `OTP_CODES_RETENTION_HOURS`, each with what the sweep removes.
- **Notifications card (#1840)** — says workspace-wide defaults are set by the deployment configuration, names the variables, links the notifications guide, and states delivery is *additive* (the previous text said "falls back", which `TeamsPublisher` et al. do not do — the workspace default and linked channels both deliver).
- **"No destructive workspace actions in v1"** placeholder → a **Destructive actions** card pointing each action at where it lives (Admin → Suites, Connections, Members, Compliance; retention for run history).
- `DOCS_URL` moved from `App.tsx` to `utils/docs.ts` so pages can link the published guides.

**Backend (additive)** — `GET /admin/workspace-config` (Admin-gated by the `/admin` router dependency), returning the retention clocks and allowlists as deployed; `membership_service.configured_allowlists()` is the public wrapper over the gates the sign-in doors actually read, so the `active` flag can never disagree with the door. It is a config read with no regulated data, so it has no entry in the G1 audit/access coverage tables (both guards pass). OpenAPI export and the generated Python client regenerated (rule 45).

## Verification

- Backend: `black --check`, `ruff`, `mypy backend/app backend/tests`, `bandit`, full `pytest backend/tests` against a private test DB — __BACKEND__
- Frontend: `pnpm lint`, `tsc --noEmit`, `pnpm test:coverage`, `pnpm build` — __FRONTEND__
- `python -m backend.scripts.export_docs_reference` + `scripts/generate-dataq-client.py --check` clean with ruff 0.16.5 on PATH.
- No `placeholder` / `post-v1` / `follow-up` UI text remains in `frontend/src` (the only hits are HTML `placeholder=` attributes and a code comment).
- No new `<Route>`, so `e2e-demo/routes.ts` is unchanged; the new request on `/admin/settings` is recorded automatically.

## Accessibility (rule 44)

Profile card titles are headings under the page's `h3`; the owned-suites list has `aria-label="Suites you own"`; the access summary and the retention list have accessible names; the allowlist table is named; every status is worded (colour is additional, never the only carrier); inline links use `.dq-text-link`; external docs links open in a new tab with `rel="noreferrer"`.

## Docs

`docs/site/guides/admin.md` (page map + four new Settings sections), `docs/site/guides/features.md` (Profile), `changelog.d/1516.changed.md`, `changelog.d/1840.fixed.md`.

Fixes #1516

    """Batch `effective_permission` for many suites in one shares query (no N+1)."""

    if shared_ids:
        rows = session.scalars(

        levels = {row.suite_id: row.permission for row in rows}
